## The models

**Single trait** (nested data with a `value` column, or `traits = "adg"`):

```text
asreml(value ~ <fixed>,
       random   = ~ vm(id, relmat) + <random>,
       residual = ~ idv(units), dense = ~ vm(id, relmat), ...)
```

**Two traits** (`value1` + `value2`, or `traits = c("a", "b")`):

```text
asreml(cbind(value1, value2) ~ trait + trait:<fixed>,
       random   = ~ <genetic_cov>(trait):vm(id, relmat) + <random_cov>(trait):<random>,
       residual = ~ units:<residual_cov>(trait), dense = ~ <genetic_cov>(trait):vm(id, relmat), ...)
```

| argument | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `fixed` | one-sided formula, e.g. `~ hhys + sex` | `~ 1` |
| `random` | further random effects, e.g. `~ ide(id)`, `~ litter + pen` | none |
| `genetic_cov` | `"us"`, `"idh"` / `"diag"`, `"corv"`, `"corh"`, `"corgh"` | `"us"` |
| `random_cov` | same, applied to every term of `random` | `"us"` |
| `residual_cov` | `"us"`, `"idh"` / `"diag"` | `"us"` |
| `na_x` | `na.method(x = )`: `"include"`, `"fail"`, `"omit"` | `"include"` |
| `asreml_args` | further `asreml()` arguments | `list()` |

Some common choices:

```{r}
# repeated records: permanent environment, otherwise h2 is inflated
asr_gblup(param, cv, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, random = ~ ide(id))

# litter effect, uncorrelated between traits
asr_gblup(param, cv, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, random = ~ litter, random_cov = "idh")

# us() is hard to fit: correlation parameterisation
asr_gblup(param, cv, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, genetic_cov = "corgh")

# one trait in two herds: nobody has both records -> diag residual, no rp
asr_gblup(param, cv, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, traits = c("bfs", "nls"),
          genetic_cov = "corgh", residual_cov = "diag", rp = FALSE)
```

## Why not `V1 / (V1 + V2)`?

`vpredict()` refers to the variance parameters as `V1`, `V2`, ... in the order
of the `vparameters` component of the fit. That order depends on the model:

| model | V1 | V2 | V3 | V4 | V5 | V6 | V7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| us G + us R | V~a,1~ | Cov~a~ | V~a,2~ | `units:trait!R` = 1 | V~e,1~ | Cov~e~ | V~e,2~ |
| corgh G + diag R | r~a~ | V~a,1~ | V~a,2~ | `units:trait!R` = 1 | V~e,1~ | V~e,2~ | - |
| us G + idh litter + us R | V~a,1~ | Cov~a~ | V~a,2~ | V~c,1~ | V~c,2~ | `units:trait!R` | ... |

The formula `rg ~ V2 / sqrt(V1 * V3)` is right for the first model, wrong for
the second (V1 is already the correlation) and `rp` with `V7` fails. So
mintyrasr reads the **names** of the components and builds the formulas
itself.

## How components are recognised

Each row of `summary(fit)$varcomp` is matched to `names(fit$vparameters)`
(the `V` number) and classified:

| name (examples) | term | role | kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vm(id, relmat)` | `vm(id, relmat)` | genetic | var |
| `ide(id)`, `litter` | itself | random | var |
| `units!units` | `units` | residual | var |
| `units!R` after `units!units` (idv), `units:trait!R` | | | scale = 1, not used |
| `trait:vm(id, relmat)!trait_adg:adg` | `trait:vm(id, relmat)` | genetic | var |
| `trait:vm(id, relmat)!trait_bf:adg` | | genetic | cov |
| `trait:litter!trait_adg` | `trait:litter` | random | var (idh) |
| `...!trait!bf:!trait!adg.cor`, `...!trait!cor` | | | cor (corgh, corh, corv) |
| `...!trait!var` | | | var shared by both traits (corv) |
| `fa(...)`, `rr(...)` terms | | | not interpreted (warning) |

Inside the model the relationship matrix is called `relmat`, so components
read `vm(id, relmat)`. (With the name `ginv`, ASReml-R 4.2 crashes for an
`ainverse()` matrix in a formula built inside a function.) In `random` you can
still write `vm(dam, ginv)`; output names such as `prop_vm_dam_ginv` keep
`ginv`.

Trait names are found as whole words in the name, so any column name works.
The `vc_index` table of the result shows the classification - look at it
after the first run of a new model.

## Notation

Symbols in the text are written with sub- and superscripts; the output uses
plain column names:

| symbol | meaning | in the output |
|---|---|---|
| h², h²~i~ | heritability (of trait *i*) | `h2`, `h2_<trait>` |
| r~g~, r~p~ | genetic, phenotypic correlation | `rg`, `rp` |
| r~B~ | type-B genetic correlation between environments | `rB_<X>` |
| V~a~, V~e~, V~p~ | additive genetic, residual, phenotypic variance | `va` (per fold) |
| V~a,1~, V~p,2~ | the variance of trait 1, trait 2 | |
| Cov~a~, Cov~e~ | genetic, residual covariance of the two traits | |
| c², pe², m² | litter, permanent environment, maternal genetic proportion | `prop_<term>` |
| A⁻¹, G⁻¹, H⁻¹ | inverse pedigree, genomic, single-step relationship matrix | argument `ginv` |
| `V1`, `V2`, ... | **labels** of the variance parameters used by `vpredict()`, not subscripts | `vc_index$V` |

## The formulas

For each trait *i*, with V~p,i~ = the sum of **all** used variances of that
trait (genetic + other random + residual):

- **h²~i~** = V~a,i~ / V~p,i~
- **r~g~** = Cov~a~ / √(V~a,1~ V~a,2~); for `corv` / `corh` / `corgh` the
  correlation parameter itself
- **r~p~** = (sum of all covariances) / √(V~p,1~ V~p,2~); the covariance of a
  correlation-parameterised term is written as r√(V~1~V~2~)

Examples of what is generated (`param$formulas`):

```
# single trait, G + e
h2 = V1/(V1 + V2)
# single trait, G + pe + e
h2 = V1/(V1 + V2 + V3)
# us G + us R
h2_value1 = V1/(V1 + V5); rg = V2/sqrt(V1 * V3); rp = (V2 + V6)/sqrt((V1 + V5) * (V3 + V7))
# corgh G + diag R, one trait in two herds
h2_nls = V2/(V2 + V5); h2_bfs = V3/(V3 + V6); rg = V1
```

## Your own formulas

Anything else - repeatability, litter proportion, maternal or total
heritability - goes into `vpredict`, as a named list. Check the `V` numbers
in `vc_index` first; they depend on the model.

```{r}
res <- asr_gblup(param, cv, ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, random = ~ ide(id),
                 vpredict = list(rep = rep ~ (V1 + V2) / (V1 + V2 + V3)))
res$vc_index
res$param[, c("h2", "h2_se", "rep", "rep_se")]
```

Models with more than one genetic term (e.g. maternal `str()` models) and
`fa()` / `rr()` structures need their own formulas: the automatic ones only
use the term `vm(<id>, relmat)`.

## Tests

| argument | full model | reduced model | `lrt()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_rg = TRUE` (default) | as specified | genetic structure `idh(trait)`, the rest unchanged | `boundary = FALSE` (0 is not on the boundary of a correlation) |
| `test_rp = TRUE` | as specified | `idh` for the genetic, extra random and residual terms | `boundary = FALSE`; `cov_df` = number of covariances |

`test_rp` asks whether the two traits are correlated at all; it is not a test
of r~p~ = 0 on its own. Results: `rg_lrt`, `rg_p`, `cov_df`, `cov_lrt`, `cov_p`
in `param`.

## Checks and warnings

- `ginv` without `attr(, "INVERSE") = TRUE`: `vm()` would treat it as G.
- Individuals with phenotypes that are not in `ginv`.
- Components fixed at the boundary (bound `B`): warning and `param$boundary`.
- `asreml.options(gammaPar = TRUE)`: the automatic formulas assume the
  default variance (sigma) parameterisation.
- Fits that did not converge (`max_update` to call `update()`).
